name: Lemper Cooking Competition
description: Pak Chanek is participating in a lemper cooking competition. In the competition, Pak Chanek has to cook lempers with $$$N$$$ stoves that are arranged sequentially from stove $$$1$$$ to stove $$$N$$$. Initially, stove $$$i$$$ has a temperature of $$$A_i$$$ degrees. A stove can have a negative temperature. Pak Chanek realises that, in order for his lempers to be cooked, he needs to keep the temperature of each stove at a non-negative value. To make it happen, Pak Chanek can do zero or more operations. In one operation, Pak Chanek chooses one stove $$$i$$$ with $$$2 \leq i \leq N-1$$$, then: changes the temperature of stove $$$i-1$$$ into $$$A_{i-1} := A_{i-1} + A_{i}$$$, changes the temperature of stove $$$i+1$$$ into $$$A_{i+1} := A_{i+1} + A_{i}$$$, and changes the temperature of stove $$$i$$$ into $$$A_i := -A_i$$$. Pak Chanek wants to know the minimum number of operations he needs to do such that the temperatures of all stoves are at non-negative values. Help Pak Chanek by telling him the minimum number of operations needed or by reporting if it is not possible to do.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$N$$$ ($$$1 \le N \le 10^5$$$) — the number of stoves. The second line contains $$$N$$$ integers $$$A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N$$$ ($$$-10^9 \leq A_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the initial temperatures of the stoves.
output_specification: Output an integer representing the minimum number of operations needed to make the temperatures of all stoves at non-negative values or output $$$-1$$$ if it is not possible.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1725L — Lemper Cooking Competition [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
